findings.description: contracts/openapi/v1.1.yaml constrains ExcludedAssignment.reason to the regex pattern '^(lane|policy|catalog|roadmap|registry|cedar):[a-z0-9-]+$'. However, existing dg-00 resolver code in agent-coordinator/src/model_routing/resolver.py:160-166 produces exclusion reasons 'unavailable' (when not cand.available) and 'quota:exhausted' (when cand.quota_headroom_pct <= 0). Neither reason matches the pattern ('unavailable' has no prefix, and 'quota' is omitted from the allowed prefix set). Neither design.md nor tasks.md specifies normalizing these reasons in resolver.py to match the new prefix vocabulary (e.g. catalog:unavailable, catalog:quota-exhausted) or widening the regex pattern, which causes responses with catalog exclusions to fail OpenAPI contract validation.

Design D10 asserts that 'PostgreSQL coverage proves the additive JSONB decision round trip and durable audit link.' However, work-packages.yaml contains no package verification step that runs against a live PostgreSQL database. In wp-policy-service, test_routing_audit.py is grouped with unit tests, and in wp-integration, the coordinator regression explicitly excludes integration tests with -m 'not e2e and not integration'. Because real database tests in this repository live under tests/integration/postgres/ and require PostgreSQL, migration 042's atomic decision and audit RPC has no executable acceptance evidence anywhere in the work package pipeline.

findings.description: routing.schema.json fallback object requires location_order and isolation_order, but omits dispatch_mode_order. While defaults specifies global and phase dispatch defaults, design D8 specifies that local fallback deterministically selects among the lane's exact configured values when the coordinator is unreachable. When an agents.yaml lane configures multiple cli.dispatch_modes (e.g. review, alternative, quick) and the phase default is unsupported by that lane, the local fallback helper lacks a defined fallback order in routing.yaml to deterministically select the dispatch mode.

Design D7 requires that 'No raw secret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list enters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.' While spec.md specifies that persistence excludes legacy extras, contracts/openapi/v1.1.yaml defines task_signals with additionalProperties: true and defines no separate PersistedRequest schema. In current implementation, api.py stores request.model_dump() directly into JSONB without an allowlist filter. Without an explicit schema contract for the persisted request projection, redaction remains prose-only and unenforced by contract tests.

Design D8 specifies that skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py validates routing.yaml against its schema. However, contracts/config/routing.schema.json is located in the coordinator/openspec directory, which is absent in consumer repository installations where only skills/ is installed (verified by test_consumer_portability.py). The write_allow for wp-transports-fallback does not permit vendoring or locating the schema within skills/shared/, leaving routing_fallback.py without access to its validation schema in portable skill environments.

VendorRegistryService._snapshots (vendor_registry.py:340-357) emits a vendor_catalog_projection_miss audit event and warning for every unprojected or ambiguous lane-model on every invocation. Calling it on every routing request per design D4 means persistent catalog gaps will generate audit log entries on every select_model request. Design D4 should clarify whether RoutingService suppresses projection miss audit events or uses a cached registry snapshot to avoid swamping the audit log.

findings.description: The file contracts/events/routing-decision.schema.json declares $id as routing-audit-link-v1.schema.json and title as 'Durable routing decision audit link'. While contracts/README.md documents that it defines the link-only coordinator audit event, naming the file routing-decision.schema.json creates confusion with the primary routing_decisions table row schema. Aligning the filename to routing-audit-link.schema.json would improve readability and consistency.
